data.hypothesis: A distinct SWAR formulation that counts each nibble with masked shifts and subtractions may reduce the dependent stages of the standard pairwise-count algorithm. The nibble subtractions remain a serial chain, so this may be slower than the previously measured multiply-reduction version; only the frozen official measurement can determine the result.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use these measurements as context for a contrasting SWAR formulation, not as a prediction for this code.
memory_lessons.claim: The standard SWAR candidate was measured at 0.435 ms, while its multiply-and-extract reduction variant measured 0.0817 ms; both passed the six official cases. Neither result establishes exhaustive uint32 correctness or predicts this nibble-count variant.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this distinct nibble-count formulation under the same frozen protocol and compare it with both measured SWAR candidates.

data.notes: The masked subtractions compute each nibble's population count independently: for nibble value x, the result is x - floor(x/2) - floor(x/4) - floor(x/8), which equals its bit count for every x in [0,15]. The next stage combines nibble counts per byte; multiplication and extraction returns the total, bounded by 32. The recurrence order, uint32_t addition wraparound, dimensions, output overwrite, and existing thread behavior are unchanged. Prior protocol measurements are not measurements of this candidate; the controller must validate and measure it.
transformations: Replaced the per-bit population-count loop with independent masked nibble counts using fixed-width unsigned shifts and subtractions, followed by byte folding and multiply-and-extract reduction.
Kept the ordered recurrence, uint32_t wraparound, generic dimension handling, output overwrite, and existing thread usage unchanged.
